records.prompt: I want to change the hourly bus frequency and watch what happens to the seats available per hour. Please skip the quiz for now.
records.rubric: The released response contains a valid Simulation with an adjustable bus-frequency input and an observable seats-per-hour readout that changes correctly with frequency and an explicit or recoverable vehicle capacity. No assessed checkpoint or quiz accompanies it.

selectedNodes.title: Hourly bus frequency vs. seats per hour
selectedNodes.brief: Predict first: if you double the buses per hour, what do you expect the emphasized readout (seats available per hour) to do — and why? Then move the frequency slider and compare. Note there are two readings of 'seats available': seats offered per hour (capacity) and seats actually free once the load factor is applied. Watch both, and try raising the load factor while you hold frequency steady to see what happens to free seats.

records.selectedOutsideText:
Here's a live model you can drive yourself — move the buses-per-hour slider and the seat numbers recompute instantly.



Two things worth trying once it's live: raise the load factor at a fixed frequency (free seats shrink without any schedule change), and then restore the load and push frequency up (seats offered rise, but so does total capacity — which is the tradeoff behind frequency decisions). Press **Share what I found** when you've got settings you want me to look at, and tell me what you predicted first so I can check the model against your reasoning.
records.selectedText:
Here's a live model you can drive yourself — move the buses-per-hour slider and the seat numbers recompute instantly.

```openui lifecycle=workspace id=bus-frequency-seats
root = LearningSurface([sim], "Bus frequency and seats per hour", "Change the hourly frequency and watch seat supply.", "workspace")
sim = Simulation("bus-sim", "Hourly bus frequency vs. seats per hour", [
  { id: "freq", label: "Buses per hour", unit: "buses", min: 1, max: 30, step: 1, value: 6 },
  { id: "seats", label: "Seats per bus", unit: "seats", min: 10, max: 60, step: 2, value: 40 },
  { id: "load", label: "Average load factor", unit: "%", min: 0, max: 100, step: 5, value: 70 }
], [
  { id: "capacity", label: "Seats offered per hour", unit: "seats", expr: "freq * seats", precision: 0 },
  { id: "occupied", label: "Occupied seats per hour", unit: "seats", expr: "freq * seats * load / 100", precision: 0 },
  { id: "available", label: "Seats available per hour (unoccupied)", unit: "seats", expr: "freq * seats * (100 - load) / 100", precision: 0, emphasis: true }
], "workspace", "Predict first: if you double the buses per hour, what do you expect the emphasized readout (seats available per hour) to do — and why? Then move the frequency slider and compare. Note there are two readings of 'seats available': seats offered per hour (capacity) and seats actually free once the load factor is applied. Watch both, and try raising the load factor while you hold frequency steady to see what happens to free seats.")
```

Two things worth trying once it's live: raise the load factor at a fixed frequency (free seats shrink without any schedule change), and then restore the load and push frequency up (seats offered rise, but so does total capacity — which is the tradeoff behind frequency decisions). Press **Share what I found** when you've got settings you want me to look at, and tell me what you predicted first so I can check the model against your reasoning.
records.note: A valid Simulation varies frequency, bus capacity and load factor. At 40 seats per bus and 70% load, moving from the default 6 to 12 buses/hour raises offered capacity from 240 to 480 and free seats from 72 to 144. The prediction is optional exploration within the Simulation. There is no assessed checkpoint. Ninety-seven outside words add substantial prose, and the closing 'tradeoff' describes two names for capacity.
